pcs.pc_description: receive work instructions and technical drawings from the supervisor or network engineers to plan for LAN/WAN installation.
identify and select appropriate network devices (such as, routers, modems, switches, patch panels) based on network layout and capacity requirements.
interpret circuit diagrams, IP schemas, and cable routing plans before setting up the hardware.
unbox and inspect network hardware for physical damages or missing components as per BOM (Bill of Material).

modules.module_title: Set up LAN and WAN hardware components

pcs.pc_description: connect routers, switches, and wireless access points as per standard layer 2 and layer 3 network architecture.
assign correct ports and label all connections (e.g., uplink/downlink, VLAN ID, WAN/LAN) for traceability.
configure basic network parameters such as ip address, subnet mask, default gateway, and dns settings on routers and switches.
install and configure access points (APS) with ssid, channel, and security settings in compliance with organisational standards.
establish uplinks to the Internet Service Provider (ISP) gateway and verify link synchronisation.

modules.module_title: Ensure proper network cabling and configuration

pcs.pc_description: identify suitable cable types (cat5e, cat6, fibre optic) based on network bandwidth and distance requirements.
measure, cut, and crimp ethernet cables using appropriate tools (e.g., cable stripper, crimping tool, rj45 connectors).
install network cables in ducts, raceways, or conduits ensuring minimal bending and no physical strain on connectors.
label both ends of each cable using cable tags or colour codes for easy fault diagnosis.
check grounding and bonding of racks and metal equipment to avoid electrical hazards.
power up the devices and verify boot status through indicator leds or diagnostic ports.
use basic network testing tools (e.g., lan tester, cable certifier, TDR meter) to ensure cable integrity and proper connectivity.
perform ping test , speed test, and bandwidth tests to confirm desired connectivity and speed.
take photograph and record test results in the job sheet or digital installation report.

modules.module_title: Take instructions and prepare for installation tasks

pcs.pc_description: verify availability of hardware such as managed/unmanaged switches, layer 2 or layer 3 routers, cables, connectors, and power supply.
ensure all tools required for the setup (such as, crimping tool, cable tester, punch-down tool, screwdrivers) are ready and functional.
assess network design documents or topology diagrams to understand IP allocation, switch roles, and VLAN structure.

modules.module_title: Install and physically set up network devices

pcs.pc_description: mount the switch or router securely in racks or wall enclosures as per standard procedures.
verify cable continuity using LAN cable testers and ensure colour coding or labelling of ports for traceability.
connect network cables (Cat5e/Cat6 or fibre) to appropriate switch/router ports following the assigned port plan.
connect power cables, backup power sources (e.g., UPS), and confirm device boot-up through LED indicators or diagnostics.
access the switch/router console via serial/USB port or IP-based terminal software (e.g., PuTTY, Tera Term).
assign static or dynamic IP addresses to devices based on DHCP settings or static routing plans.
configure basic settings such as hostname, domain name, password protection, and NTP synchronisation.
create and assign VLANs, configure trunk and access ports, and verify inter-VLAN routing if applicable.
enable port security features, MAC address filtering, and spanning tree protocol (STP) to avoid network loops.
configure routers with gateway IP, NAT/PAT settings, routing protocols (e.g., RIP, OSPF), and route summarisation.
set up access control lists (ACLs) to manage data flow and apply firewall rules to restrict unauthorised traffic.
verify connectivity through ping and traceroute commands.
run interface status and routing table commands (e.g., show ip int brief, show vlan, show run) to confirm operational parameters.
troubleshoot configuration issues by checking log files, LED indicators, and loopback test results.
back up device configurations to external storage or network drive using TFTP/FTP or USB.

modules.module_title: Receive Work Instructions and Prepare for Maintenance

pcs.pc_description: review the network layout diagram, device inventory, and location plan to identify devices due for inspection or servicing.
ensure possession of all required tools and diagnostic equipment such as multimeters, LAN testers, OTDRs, crimping tools, and splicing kits.
verify stock availability of spare parts like SFP modules, connectors, patch cords, power supplies, and batteries required for field replacement.
perform a visual inspection of the assigned site for safety hazards and access points before starting work.

modules.module_title: Inspect, Diagnose and Troubleshoot Network Devices

pcs.pc_description: inspect active network devices (e.g., routers, switches, access points, ONU/ONT) for signs of wear, physical damage, loose connections, or overheating.
run diagnostic tests to check device health indicators such as port activity, LED status, temperature logs, and fan operations.
identify connectivity issues, signal degradation, or packet loss using ping tests, cable continuity checks, and loopback tests.
assess power supply units and backup systems (e.g., UPS, PoE injectors) for consistent voltage output and battery health.
check fibre patch panels and copper patch cords for proper insertion, labelling, and potential microbends or cable stress.

modules.module_title: Carry Out Maintenance Tasks and Replace Faulty Components

pcs.pc_description: clean optical ports, connectors, and device enclosures using standard cleaning kits and ESD- safe materials.
tighten loose terminations, replace damaged connectors, and realign misconfigured port connections as per standard guidelines.
update or reconfigure firmware/software settings on CPEs and switches, if required, using vendor-specific CLI/GUI interfaces.
replace non-functional components such as power adaptors, SFP modules, fan units, or fuses with compatible spare parts.
perform minor field-level splicing of fibre drop cables using hand tools or portable fusion splicers to restore link continuity.

modules.module_title: Test and Validate Network Performance Post- Maintenance

pcs.pc_description: test the link throughput, signal strength, latency, and packet loss after repair using handheld testers or mobile apps.
confirm network stability by checking interface up/down status, IP assignment, and device reachability via ping or traceroute.
ensure customer or user devices (e.g., routers, STBs, IP phones) are synchronised with the network and receiving consistent bandwidth.
record the maintenance activities, replaced items, and device health metrics in physical or digital logs as per organisational format.
report completion status and any unresolved issues to the supervisor or escalate if specialised support is needed.

modules.module_title: Maintain an organised, productive, and digitally compliant workspace

follow designated workflow as per the organisational Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)

track and update digital task checklists, inventories, or handovers through mobile/desktop apps

use personal protective equipment (PPE) such as ESD wrist straps, gloves, masks, and safety footwear
